The game overall just feels quite underbaked. A lot of the top's abilities are downright trash, completely broken, or are hard to use. The controls feel wonky and unresponsive. The item variety is nonexistent. The bosses and minibosses feel less like a challenge and more like a slog (I made it to the third boss on my first ever run, which only ended because the game crashed halfway through the battle).

The gameplay is a slog broken up by the AI occasionally flying out of the arena from a light nudge, all the visual flair (which can thankfully be toggled off, except for the constant momentum-grinding slowdown on impacts) actively makes things more muddy and hard to follow, and the dialogue is written with the vibes of a greasy English-second-language child who's deeply sexually fixated on the clown girl from Amazing Digital Circus. This is still in the top three best Beyblade videogames.

Game is actually really fun, it’s quite hard and there were a lot of times where I felt I lost due to factors completely out of my control but it always felt like I could boot it back up and try to come up with a strategy to get through. There’s genuine skill barriers which is great. My biggest criticism is the lack of customization, I’ll be honest being able to make customized tops was almost the entire reason I was interested in this game to begin with, but as far as I can tell that feature is just completely missing from the game despite being advertised, and for that reason I just can’t recommend the game. If you choose to continue updating, my biggest ask would be a map encounter that lets you swap parts, other than that it’s a pretty great little indie game that’s just missing a big feature that you’ve advertised on the store page.

MAYBE I'm doing something wrong, but I kinda hate it. Love the concept/idea, but the gameplay just isn't for me. Probably a skill issue but I cannot grasp the combat and it's frustrating. It almost feels like theres a type chart variant that exists but I can't figure out what it could be. Doesn't help that the tutorial doesn't explain the combat enough, and spends too much time showing off the "quirky" character and its dumb dialogue. Some levels I destroy with no issue, others I get totally rolled. Again, you could argue skill is needed here and I don't have that which is fair, but I dunno. For example, I felt frustrated fighting the guard shield. I could tell the counter was to attack it while its shield was down but I just felt annoyed fighting against it. Same with the Lone Vampire. I cannot figure out the counter to it as I'm writing this, and the health stealing effect is just too frustrating. Gaining back like 25 out of its 60 health when it kills you is so stupid. I love roguelikes and I know if I could understand this game more I might like it, but at this moment I don't. I'm just disappointed.

I reaaaally wanted to like this game. i grew up with beyblade and i like the art style and soundtrack a lot. Unfortunately, in practice the gameplay is really inconsistent, the controls are jank, and the difficulty curve goes from very difficult to mindnumbingly easy instantly. Once you get the top that floats you're basically unbeatable. Don't get me wrong, the powertrip is fun, but I found myself having more fun spitefully crushing the game itself more than any of the tops in it. I'd say check this game out if you want to play a decent beyblade video game, but prepare to be frustrated.

The game is a lot of fun once it opens up and you have lots of tops to experiment with. For anyone struggling with the first boss, anything with a high attack will let you bully them so long as it has more than 25 stamina. My one gripe is that certain tops only appear on specific floors. Which as a strategic choice makes sense for experienced players who then can plan runs. But I think a better solution would be to have stocks for certain tops have a higher chance of them showing up on certain floors. Adding more of that high when you luck out and see something rare early in a run.

The game is... okay. For the price it's worth it but the game feels more like a demo to show off a cool concept rather than a full game. The artstyle while cool relies too heavily on a strong dithering filter; if the artstyle was instead sculpted with a less heavy dithering effect in mind I think it would have been much better. The tutorial could have also been a lot more streamlined, the way it is presented makes the player able to accidentally miss one very important bit of information if they look away for a short moment then need to restart the whole tutorial over again to see what they missed. Some sort of text log would be an easy fix for that. The content itself is fun but very short, you can experience everything with one or two quick playthroughs. The balancing itself is also not the greatest with certain combinations being instant wins and too easily acquirable. With all of this taken into consideration I don't think the game is bad but I don't think it's good. What saves it from being bad is how cheap the game is makes it hard to argue that the purchase is regrettable. I've seen the teasers for the second game of the same concept and I have to say I am much more excited for that as it looks more like an actual game than a short demo. While I can't exactly in good conscious leave a bad review for this game as it's so cheap I would suggest skipping this and waiting for the next game instead unless you are really fiending for a taste of what's to come.
